songInfo.title: Simple Man
songInfo.tuning: Half-Step Down (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb)

scalesUsed.notes: A - B - C - D - E - F - G - A
scalesUsed.application: Forms the foundation of the iconic C - G - Am arpeggiated intro and verse progression (sounding a half-step lower in G#m)

scalesUsed.notes: A - C - D - E - G - A
scalesUsed.application: Used for Gary Rossington's crying, sustain-rich Les Paul lead fills and guitar solo

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Reflective, hymn-like C major to A natural minor descending bassline progression with heavy Southern blues-rock weight
keyAndScale.keySignature: 0 sharps/flats (in fretboard shapes; sounds in B major / G# minor due to Eb tuning)
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: A minor is the relative minor of C major

mainProgression.progressionDescription: Unchanging, cyclical three-chord Southern rock foundation (C - G - Am) where the bass walks smoothly down from C (3rd fret A) through B (2nd fret A) to the open A minor root.
mainProgression.description: Unchanging, cyclical three-chord Southern rock foundation (C - G - Am) where the bass walks smoothly down from C (3rd fret A) through B (2nd fret A) to the open A minor root.

sectionProgressions.description: Clean sixteenth-note arpeggiated picking pattern with a melodic walk-in on the A string (0-2-3)

sectionProgressions.section: Chorus ('Be a simple kind of man')
sectionProgressions.description: Heavy distorted Gibson Les Paul power chords and open voicings locking in with the drums
Soaring A minor pentatonic lead solo with expressive whole-step bends and wide Southern rock vibrato
A minor pentatonic & natural minor melodic lead phrasing

harmonicFunction: C (bIII) - Bright relative major opening chord that sets an uplifting, maternal tone
G / G/B (bVII) - Passing dominant-function chord creating a smooth stepwise bass descent (C → B → A)
Am (i) - Soulful minor tonic where each two-bar phrase settles for two full measures

techniques.name: Cross-Picked Clean Arpeggios & Bass Walk-Ins
techniques.description: Picking individual notes across open C, G, and Am chord shapes while maintaining a steady sixteenth-note pulse and connecting cycles with an A-string bass walk-up (0-2-3)

sequence: Walk up on the A string (open A → 2nd fret B → 3rd fret C) to launch the C major chord
Arpeggiate from the bass strings up to the B and G strings and back down
Shift to G major and repeat the arpeggio pattern
Land on A minor for two full measures, adding little melodic extensions on the 3rd fret of the B and high E strings
tips: Hold the full chord shape down so each plucked note rings into the next like a harp
Use alternate picking (Down-Up) as you cross between the D, G, and B strings
In the chorus, kick on your overdrive and hit full, authoritative power chords

sections.name: Intro & Verse Arpeggio Pattern
sections.description: The timeless clean arpeggiated intro walking up into C, stepping down through G, and resting on Am.
notes: Keep all notes ringing together across each chord
Play the A-string 0-2-3 walk-up cleanly into beat 1
Maintain a steady 60 BPM sixteenth-note feel

sections.name: Heavy Chorus Power Chords
sections.description: Thick, roaring C, G, and A5 chords driving the chorus ('And be a simple kind of man').
notes: Switch to your bridge humbucker with rich tube overdrive
Let the chords sustain for two beats each on C and G, then four beats on Am
Add rhythmic palm-muted chugs before changing chords

sections.name: A Minor Pentatonic Lead Phrase
sections.description: Expressive A minor pentatonic solo phrase in 5th position with crying bends and wide vibrato.
notes: Support your ring-finger bends on the 7th fret G string with your index and middle fingers
Apply slow, wide vibrato on long sustained notes
Target the root note A on the 7th fret of the D string

guitar.recommended: Fender Stratocaster (Ed King clean intro) & 1959 Gibson Les Paul Standard (Gary Rossington)
guitar.pickup: Stratocaster neck pickup for clean arpeggios; Les Paul bridge PAF humbucker for chorus and solo

effects.distortion: Natural tube amp overdrive or Boss SD-1 Super OverDrive
effects.other: Heavy guitar pick for authoritative arpeggio and power-chord attack

beginner.title: Three-Chord Cycle & Bass Walk
steps: Master the open C, G, and Am chord shapes
Practice the A-string 0-2-3 bass walk-up into the C chord
Strum C (2 beats) → G (2 beats) → Am (4 beats) smoothly at 60 BPM

intermediate.title: Note-for-Note Clean Arpeggio Picking
steps: Pick the exact sixteenth-note arpeggio pattern across C, G, and Am without looking at your picking hand
Add the 3rd-fret high-E and B-string pinky embellishments on the Am chord
Transition cleanly from delicate verse arpeggios to heavy chorus power chords

advanced.title: Expressive A Minor Soloing
steps: Learn the A minor pentatonic solo phrases in 5th, 8th, and 12th positions
Execute multi-step bends and wide, vocal-like vibrato
Improvise your own Southern rock outro solo over the C - G - Am progression

commonMistakes: Lifting fingers off the chord shape too early, cutting off the arpeggio sustain
Rushing the slow 60 BPM tempo during the quiet verses
Using only downstrokes during string-crossing arpeggios instead of efficient alternate picking
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: A-string 0-2-3 walk-up into clean C → G → Am chord changes
5 minutes: Isolated sixteenth-note arpeggio picking pattern at 50 BPM → 60 BPM
5 minutes: Chorus power chords and dynamic switching
5 minutes: A minor pentatonic soloing over a backing track
focusAreas: Letting all arpeggiated notes ring together
Expressive vibrato and bend intonation in the solo
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 60 BPM and feel eighth-note and sixteenth-note subdivisions
Ensure the 0-2-3 walk-up lands squarely on beat 1 of the C chord
Keep the heavy chorus strums locked to the slow backbeat
